summary: OrbitCare (Orbitspace) is an offline-first health dashboard for astronauts on long-duration missions, where Earth is minutes away by radio and there is no hospital. It follows three astronauts across a simulated 180-day mission, comparing each day's resting heart rate, heart-rate variability, sleep, blood oxygen and bone density against that astronaut's own first-21-day baseline. Direction-aware anomaly scores feed four domain scores — Heart, Bone & Muscle, Sleep & Mind, Immune/Radiation — the crew view always shows the worst-off astronaut first, every flag carries its evidence and a plain-language action plan, and a PDF health report can be handed over to Earth. On Day 63, Kenji declines to Watch (79/100) and recovers to Nominal (95/100) by Day 90. All data is simulated and clearly labelled; OrbitCare is decision support only, not a medical device.
details:
OrbitCare is a working web app. The Crew View ranks the three astronauts worst-first by overall health score, with Nominal / Watch / Alert status chips. The Astronaut Dashboard shows each day's vitals against the astronaut's personal 21-day baseline, the four domain scores, and every active flag with its evidence. Trends charts show vitals against the normal band with a mission-day slider (1-180) and Play. The Action Plan turns each flag into plain-language steps and a downloadable health report. A daily self-check (sleep, mood, stress, symptoms) feeds the Sleep & Mind score. Everything works offline from a local cache, and a one-tap Emergency Guide covers six situations with a 110 bpm CPR metronome.

How it works: 540 simulated daily readings (3 crew x 180 days) with injected events, including Kenji's Day-63 infection. Each indicator gets a direction-aware z-score against the personal baseline, smoothed over 3 days into domain scores; Watch starts at 1, Alert at 2. Flags are rule-based and auditable, so every recommendation can be traced to its numbers.

Impact: on a Mars mission, early warning matters more than treatment — OrbitCare helps a crew spot a decline days before it becomes an emergency, and gives Earth a clean handover report.

Built with: HTML/CSS/JavaScript frontend, Node.js backend, Supabase (PostgreSQL), hosted on Vercel. The backend is tested with 64 automated tests, all passing. All health data is simulated. AI tools (Muse) helped write code and text, and this is disclosed in the project README. The full 12-slide deck is in the GitHub repo.
